title: Kobalos Malware Investigation
description: Investigate and respond to a Kobalos malware infection in a high-performance computing environment.

levels.title: Introduction
levels.content:
You are a cybersecurity analyst working for a high-performance computing (HPC) organization.

Your organization has detected suspicious network activity and believes a Kobalos malware infection may be present.

Kobalos is a complex, multiplatform malware that targets HPC clusters and other high-profile systems. It is known for creating suspicious outbound connections, using systemd timers for persistence, and maintaining a low profile to avoid detection.

Your task is to investigate the infection, identify indicators of compromise, and contain the threat.

levels.title: Identify and investigate suspicious outbound connections
levels.content:
Investigate the network connections on the target host.
Identify any suspicious outbound connections.
Determine the destination IP address, port, and frequency of the connections.

The flag you need to find is the destination IP address (string) of the suspicious outbound connections.
levels.solution:
Check the system logs and network statistics for unusual outbound traffic.
The destination IP address of the suspicious outbound connections is 192.168.40.5.

hints.title: Conceptual Hint
hints.content: Malware often communicates with command and control servers. Look for unusual outbound connections.

hints.title: Directional Hint
hints.content: Use network monitoring tools to inspect active connections.

hints.title: Near-Spoiler Hint
hints.content: Run 'ss -tulnp' to list all active network connections.

levels.title: Investigate and contain the suspicious service
levels.content:
Identify the service responsible for the suspicious outbound connections.
Investigate the service's configuration and behavior.
Contain the service by stopping it and preventing it from starting at boot.

The flag you need to find is the name of the suspicious service (string).
levels.solution:
Check the systemd services and look for any unusual or recently created services.
The name of the suspicious service is lab-checkin.timer.

hints.title: Conceptual Hint
hints.content: Malware often uses system services to maintain persistence. Investigate systemd services.

hints.title: Directional Hint
hints.content: List all systemd timers to identify suspicious services.

hints.title: Near-Spoiler Hint
hints.content: Run 'systemctl list-timers --all' to list all systemd timers.

levels.title: Investigate and remove the persistence mechanism
levels.content:
Investigate the persistence mechanism used by the malware.
Identify any scheduled tasks or cron jobs that ensure the malware's persistence.
Remove the persistence mechanism to prevent the malware from restarting after a reboot.

The flag you need to find is the name of the persistence mechanism (string).
levels.solution:
Check the systemd timers and look for any unusual or recently created timers.
The name of the persistence mechanism is lab-checkin.timer.

hints.title: Conceptual Hint
hints.content: Malware often uses persistence mechanisms to survive reboots. Investigate systemd timers.

hints.title: Directional Hint
hints.content: List all systemd timers to identify persistence mechanisms.

hints.title: Near-Spoiler Hint
hints.content: Run 'systemctl list-timers --all' to list all systemd timers.
